text: Who cheats more, men or women? Let's finally answer the question that can start more arguments than politics. Because depending on what corner of the internet you're on, the answer could be either men cheat all the time or women cheat more. They just don't get caught. So today we're going to do something crazy. We're going to use actual research instead of emotions. How wild is that? And the results are actually pretty interesting. Before we even start, we need to define what cheating means. The most representative research that we have at hand is General Social Survey, which measures cheating using a question. Have you ever had sex with someone other than your husband or wife while you were married? So right off the bat, we exclude emotional cheating or cheating in a serious relationship. Only in marriage. Still, it is a good start. Overall, we have a picture where men reported the cheating rate of around 20-25%, while women reported the cheating rate of around 13-20%. So yes, based on this data, men do cheat more. But the gap is not very significant. Moreover, data broken down by age show that the gender gap narrows or even flips in younger adults before widening at older ages. At ages 18-29, women report slightly higher cheating rates than men, 11% vs. 10%. So the average cheating rate is higher for men, mainly due to the difference in cheating rate between older men and women. But this is only for married people. Is there any data on cheating in serious relationships? Turns out that there is. A peer-reviewed study published in PubMed asked people in current relationships, which could be serious long-term dating or cohabiting, not just married, whether they had engaged in sexual behavior with someone outside their relationship that could hurt it. The results? 23.2% of men and 19.2% of women reported cheating in their current relationship. So once again, men did cheat more on average, but the gap is quite small, in this case only 4%. So what is the conclusion? It does seem that men on average cheat a bit more than women. But the difference is quite small and also depends on the age group, with younger adults even showing higher cheating rates for women. So we can say that overall both men and women cheat quite a bit, roughly 1 out of 5 people self-reported cheating. And even though men do that a bit more, the difference is quite small. Don't forget that here we are talking only about physical cheating. The data on emotional cheating is way less concrete, but there is some information on it.
